newsitem.title: USA: US to appeal part of ruling freeing Robert Cochran.
newsitem.headline: US to appeal part of ruling freeing Robert Cochran.

text.p: The U.S. government on Thursday is expected to ask the full U.S. Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals to overturn a court decision to throw out all of the criminal conviction of former Stifel, Nicolaus & Co executive Robert Cochran, a reliable source said on Tuesday.

"It's expected that the appellate section will file a petition for rehearing on Thursday," said the source, referring to the U.S. Justice Department's appellate division. Justice will ask the court to overturn that part of the decision dealing with Oklahoma City Airport Trust bonds, the source said.
A three-member panel of the 10th Circuit in late March unanimously reversed a federal jury's conviction of Cochran on eight charges of wire fraud and money laundering.
The charges involved side fees Cochran allegedly made in helping issuers find a good rate on investment contracts for airport trust and the Sisters of St. Mary Healthcare System bond deals.
The panel said that Cochran did not have to disclose the fees because he was arranging the contracts on an informal basis for the authorities instead of being officially contracted to find the rates.
The appeals panel also said there is no evidence that Cochran had tried to harm the healthcare issuer because his actions did not threaten the tax-exempt status of the bonds.
The source said it is unclear whether or not the request for a rehearing by the full appeals panel, known as an "en banc" hearing, will be filed by the Justice Dept. itself or by U.S. attorneys.
